title: How a Fiber Optic Cable Works in 60 Seconds 💡🌐 #shorts
description:
A fiber optic cable carries the internet as flashes of light. A glass core about as thin as a hair is wrapped in cladding that bounces the light back inside, so it can zigzag for kilometers. Lasers blink on and off to send ones and zeros, and many colors of light can share one fiber. Follow Inside 60 for a new "how it works" explained in 60 seconds.

#fiberoptics #internet #howitworks

steps.label: Hook
steps.text: Most of the internet travels as *light*, inside glass *thinner than a hair*.

steps.label: Core
steps.text: Each fiber has a pure glass *core*, wrapped in a layer called *cladding*.

steps.label: Bounce
steps.text: Light hits the edge at a shallow angle and *bounces back in*. That's *total internal reflection*.

steps.label: Blinks
steps.text: A *laser* blinks billions of times a second. Light on is a *one*, off is a *zero*.

steps.label: Colors
steps.text: Different *colors* of light can share one fiber, each carrying its *own data*.

steps.label: Speed
steps.text: In glass, light still moves about *200,000 kilometers* every second.

steps.label: Recap
steps.text: Glass, bounce, *blink*. Follow Inside 60 for more.
